author: @jeremyfowers

evidence.api_compatibility: No breaking API changes. This is a behavioral fix to internal server model-discovery polling. No CLI flags, config values, API endpoints, or persistence formats are altered.
evidence.documentation: Documentation is not affected by this change (confirmed in PR description). No public API, CLI, or config changes to document. The header comment in directory_watcher.h was updated to reflect the macOS implementation change.
evidence.manual_release_testing: The fix changes behavior of the extra_models_dir mechanism: on macOS the kqueue watcher is replaced by FSEvents, and on Linux nested subdirectories are now inotify-watched. This affects users with nested model trees or cache repos whose refs/main points change. macOS was not exercised locally by the author (stated in the PR body), and the implementation is substantially different from the prior kqueue approach. See maintainer to-do for a macOS verification step.
evidence.post_approval_commits: No commits were added after either @Geramy's or @fl0rianr's approvals. The fourth commit (b05be4c) landed 84 minutes before the first approval and 58 minutes before the last. All four commits are by the PR author or Claude.
evidence.review: Two approvals on the final commit: @Geramy (APPROVED 2026-10-01T20:27:16Z, subject areas: sockets, mac, security, Nexus mesh compute) and @fl0rianr (APPROVED 2026-10-01T21:14:14Z, subject areas: LMX omni models, GUI, CI, smart router). @fl0rianr also filed an earlier COMMENTED review (2026-10-01T18:57:07Z) flagging that the initial nested watches included IN_CREATE without distinguishing open files, and the author addressed it in the final commit (b05be4c). @superm1 was requested as a reviewer (subject areas: ROCm, Linux packaging, security, Docker, containers, llamacpp) but never submitted a review; his absence is notable given the Linux inotify changes and overall system-level nature of the patch.
evidence.security: No credentials, network calls, or permission broadening. The Linux inotify code uses recursive_directory_iterator without follow_directory_symlink and explicitly skips symlinked directories, preventing symlink-loop watches. The macOS FSEvents stream is created once with a single path and no iteration. CoreServices is linked via CMakeLists.txt — a system framework, not a new dependency risk.
evidence.tests: Three new unit tests in test_directory_watcher.cpp: test_nested_change (pre-existing nested folder), test_new_folder_is_watched (folder created after start), test_open_file_waits_for_close (Linux-only, open file not announced until closed). The routing-policy-store test was also updated to poll for the correct policy instead of accepting any swap, and the delete-then-write workaround was removed. No existing tests were weakened or deleted. CI passed on all platforms (Linux x86/ARM64, macOS, Windows).

maintainer_todos.text: Start the server on macOS with extra_models_dir set to a directory containing nested subfolders, write a model file into one subfolder, and confirm the server's model list updates within a few seconds without any external trigger.

shout_outs.reason: Co-authored by a Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) session on all four commits, producing the substantive implementation including the macOS FSEvents rewrite, the Linux nested-watch logic, and the file-close-write deduplication.

subject: fix(server): watch extra_models_dir's nested folders on Linux and macOS (#3726)
summary: Replaces macOS DirectoryWatcher's kqueue with FSEvents for recursive monitoring, and adds inotify-based nested folder watches on Linux so that changes inside subdirectories of extra_models_dir (including cache repo refs/main updates and GGUF files written into nested model folders) are detected immediately instead of waiting for an unrelated invalidation.
verdict_reason: No reviewer on the project's subject-matter-expertise roster reviewed the macOS or Linux system-programming changes; @superm1 was requested but never responded.
